title: Indian govt approves procurement of 7.11 lakh tonnes of soybean, moong, and tur at MSP in 3 States - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
From this year, the Centre has allowed Nafed and NCCF to begin purchases without waiting for the State’s request. | Photo Credit: MUSTAFAH KK

The Indian government has approved procurement of 5.21 lakh tonnes (lt) of pulses and 1.90 lt of oilseeds at their minimum support prices (MSPs) in Uttar Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka as the fresh kharif harvest starts arriving in mandis (agricultural produce marketing committee yards). The decision will benefit growers.

Under the price support scheme (PSS), implemented by the Agriculture Ministry, the Centre’s nodal agencies, Nafed and NCCF, step in to purchase oilseeds and pulses when market prices fall below the government-declared MSPs. From this year, the Centre has allowed these agencies to begin purchases without waiting for the State’s request.

Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has approved the procurement of both pulses and oilseeds at MSP worth ₹5,547.99 crore in Uttar Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka for the 2026-27 kharif season, the ministry said in a statement.

“The decision is aimed at protecting farmers from a decline in market prices and ensuring remunerative returns for their produce, particularly for pulse and oilseed growers,” Chouhan said.

In Uttar Pradesh, 4,66,000 tonnes of tur and 6,250 tonnes of moong will be procured, while in Karnataka approval has been granted for the procurement of 1,15,500 tonnes of soyabean, 13,413 tonnes of sunflower seed and 38,250 tonnes of moong. In Telangana, 62,000 tonnes of soybean and 10,766 tonnes of moong will be procured.

The decision will provide greater economic security to farmers while encouraging domestic production of pulses and oilseeds and contributing to India’s efforts towards self-reliance in pulses and edible oils, the minister said. He assured that transparent arrangements would be made at procurement centres and payments would be made directly into farmers’ bank accounts.
